# intl-t 1.3.2

Security release. **Upgrade every `intl-t` / `@intl-t/*` package to 1.3.2.**
It also ships the 1.3.0 features, which never got release notes.

## 🔒 Security: ReDoS in message variable injection

[GHSA-rgx2-wxxf-mhq9](https://github.com/nivandres/intl-t/security/advisories/GHSA-rgx2-wxxf-mhq9) · CWE-1333

The parser behind `inject()` / `injectVariables()` could backtrack exponentially on a malformed `{…}` fragment. A few dozen characters could block the event loop for seconds or longer.

**Who is affected:** apps that pass **untrusted strings as message templates**, such as CMS entries, user-defined templates or third-party translation files. Interpolated **values** were never a vector. With your own translation files, the risk is low, but upgrade anyway.

**Fix:**

- The variable and instruction parsers now run in linear time.
- Any single `{…}` fragment longer than `MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH` (10 000 characters) is left as literal text.
- Regression tests cover the pathological inputs.

**Affected:**

| Package          | Versions            |
| ---------------- | ------------------- |
| `@intl-t/format` | `< 1.3.2`           |
| `intl-t`         | `>= 0.9.0, < 1.3.2` |

All other `@intl-t/*` packages pin `@intl-t/format` exactly, so upgrade them together.

Docs now state the trust model: **message templates are code, interpolated values are data.** Expression evaluation can be disabled with `INTL_T_DISABLED_EVAL` or `enabledEval: false`.

## Since 1.2.0 (shipped in 1.3.0)

- **@intl-t/core:**
  - New `toObject()` returns an object-typed view of a node, which React renders without the JSX patch.
- **@intl-t/format:**
  - `eval` support is detected by capability instead of presence.
  - Edge runtimes and strict CSP now fall back to plain-object nodes instead of throwing `EvalError`.
- **@intl-t/next:**
  - The request locale resolves from root params.
- **@intl-t/utils:**
  - The redirect fallback applies after the locale resolves.

## 📦 Packaging

- 1.3.0 reached npm depending on `@intl-t/*@1.2.0`. 1.3.1 republished it with the right dependency versions.
- Releases now run from CI, and each tarball is verified before publishing.
- Packages are published with npm provenance.
- 1.3.0 and 1.3.1 are deprecated in favour of 1.3.2.

## 🧪 Quality

- CI is green again: 498 tests across every package.
- React DOM tests no longer leak Happy DOM's browser `Headers` into the server suites.
